hero.title: Software and AI that knows your business.
hero.subtitle:
We design and build custom software, automate your processes, and connect Claude to your systems.
Less admin, more time for what matters.

items.question: Who has owed us money for over 30 days?
items.answer: Three partners, €3,100 in total. The largest is €1,520, overdue by 47 days. Should I draft a friendly reminder for each?

items.question: What do customers often buy together?
items.answer: The ceramic mug and the coffee beans share a basket in 38% of orders. A bundle could work well.

items.question: Who hasn't ordered from us in three months?
items.answer: 14 customers, 6 of whom used to order monthly. I can sort them by the value of their last order.

services.label: Services
services.title: How we help
services.subtitle: We start with one well-defined task, where it saves you the most time. Most projects combine two or three of these.

ai.title: AI integration with Claude
ai.description: Claude takes over the repetitive work: processes invoices, sorts email, answers customers, and picks up the phone if you need it to.

software.title: Custom business software
software.description: Customer records, inventory, production tracking, partner portals. Built for how you actually work, not the other way around.

automation.title: Process automation and AI agents
automation.description: Incoming invoices, emails, and documents land where they belong on their own. A person still approves anything important.

web.title: Websites and webshops
web.description: A fast, custom-designed site or webshop, connected to the systems behind it. Ready in days.

training.title: AI training for teams
training.description: Hands-on Claude workshops built on your own tasks. No technical background needed.

audit.title: AI assessment
audit.description: We map your workflows and show where AI saves real time and where it isn't worth it. You get a written plan.

ai.label: AI integration
ai.title: Claude works in the background.
ai.subtitle: We put Claude where the manual work piles up: from incoming invoices to customer questions and phone calls.

automations.label: A few examples of what it can take off your plate

invoices.title: Invoices and documents
invoices.description: Claude reads incoming PDF invoices and delivery notes, and checks amounts and due dates. At month end it sends them to your accountant as one tidy package.
invoices.example: At month end, Claude collects the invoices that came in, checks their details, and sends them to your accountant as one tidy package.

chase.title: Reminders
chase.description: On a schedule, it watches overdue invoices, unanswered quotes and expiring contracts. It writes a personal message for each, which you approve.
chase.example: Three invoices went overdue this week. Claude drafts a personal reminder for each, you approve, and they're sent.

inbox.title: Inbox triage
inbox.description: Reads, labels and routes incoming email to the right colleague. It drafts replies based on earlier threads and your company documents.
inbox.example: A customer asks about delivery times. Claude routes the email to the right colleague, with a draft reply attached.

reports.title: Morning brief
reports.description: Every morning it collects the numbers from your invoicing system and spreadsheets and sends a short brief to Slack or email. Anything unusual is highlighted.
reports.example: At 8 am a short brief is waiting: yesterday's revenue, overdue invoices and today's to-dos. You can ask it questions too.

support.title: Customer service assistant
support.description: Answers instantly on your website and WhatsApp, using your own knowledge base and webshop data. When it's not sure, it hands the case to your team.
support.example: At 10 pm a customer asks where their order is. Claude checks the webshop and answers right away: it arrives tomorrow.

voice.title: Phone assistant
voice.description: Answers the phone in a natural voice, Claude understands the request, and books a free slot in your calendar. After every call you get a summary of the conversation.
voice.example: A call comes in over lunch, when nobody's free. The assistant picks up in Hungarian, books an appointment, and emails you a summary.

leads.title: Leads and quotes
leads.description: Replies to new inquiries within minutes, logs them in your CRM, and drafts a quote from your price list. It can book a call too.
leads.example: An inquiry arrives for a large order. Within minutes there's a draft quote based on your price list, ready for you to check.

content.title: Content in your voice
content.description: Writes product descriptions, posts and newsletters in your voice, in Hungarian, English and German. It prepares visuals in Canva and uploads copy to your webshop.
content.example: You add 50 new products. The descriptions are done in an afternoon, in three languages, in your company's style.

automations.critter: I do all eight, by the way.

projects.label: Projects
projects.title: A few of our projects.
projects.subtitle: Click an icon to see what's behind it.

palbau.name: Pál Bau
palbau.description: A bilingual Next.js site for a general contractor building family homes in Pest county. A scroll-driven Three.js model assembles the house in six phases, and visit requests are validated with Zod and delivered by email through Resend.

solutions.title: The house builds as you scroll
solutions.body: A 3D house goes up in six steps, from foundation to terrace, so the building process makes sense at a glance.

solutions.title: Answers on the first visit
solutions.body: Six questions every home builder asks: price, schedule, payment, faults, inspections. The answers are right there on the site.

solutions.title: Show home visit requests
solutions.body: A short form lets visitors request a visit, and the request reaches the contractor by email.

solutions.title: Hungarian and English
solutions.body: The whole site is available in both languages.

gaited.name: Gaited
gaited.description: A role-based career and networking platform for equestrian professionals and brands, built on Next.js, Neon Postgres and Drizzle. Gaited has been accepted into the Nashville Entrepreneur Center's Fall 2026 PreFlight cohort.

solutions.title: Accounts for equestrians and brands
solutions.body: Sign up with email or Google, confirmed with a code, with password reset included.

solutions.title: A separate experience for each
solutions.body: Equestrians and brands see different menus and content, in light or dark mode.

solutions.title: Guided profile setup
solutions.body: A step-by-step form helps new members fill in their profile after joining, and saves everything.

solutions.title: An admin console for the team
solutions.body: Sign-up statistics, member management and a verification queue in one place, with an audit trail.

solutions.title: Privacy built in
solutions.body: Members can download their data and delete their account.

scoutingdot.name: Scoutingdot
scoutingdot.description: A multi-tenant platform for model agencies and their scouts, built on Next.js and Neon Postgres. Applicants move through a six-stage pipeline with an event log of every move, and personal links and QR cards attribute each application to its scout.

solutions.title: Six stages, one screen
solutions.body: Every applicant follows the same path: application, pre-selection, casting, board vote, onboarding, then the agency's roster.

solutions.title: Search and a shared decision
solutions.body: Applicants can be filtered by height, age and measurements. In the final vote, you can see who voted what, with their notes.

solutions.title: A personal link and card for scouts
solutions.body: Each scout gets their own application link and a card with a QR code. Anyone who applies through it is credited to them automatically.

solutions.title: Payouts and a downloadable roster
solutions.body: What scouts are owed is tracked in the same place, and the roster downloads as a spreadsheet.

motorworks.name: BP Motorworks
motorworks.description: A demo website for a Budapest car repair shop. Drivers see the services with starting prices, how the work goes and the opening hours, and find the booking form on the same page.

solutions.title: Services with starting prices
solutions.body: Six services, each with its starting price, and a clear note that the final price is set after inspection.

solutions.title: The job in four steps
solutions.body: Booking, inspection, approving the quote, pickup. Drivers know what to expect before they arrive.

solutions.title: Booking in a few fields
solutions.body: Name, phone, car model and the service needed, next to the address, map and opening hours.

solutions.title: Hungarian and English
solutions.body: The whole site works in both languages and remembers the visitor's choice.

gradio.name: Project Gradio
gradio.description: An exam prep app for Hungarian high school students, starting with history. It's a Turborepo monorepo: Next.js now, Expo for iOS and Android next, both on one type-safe tRPC API. The goal: instant marking, clear explanations, and whatever a student gets wrong comes back.

solutions.title: A waitlist for launch
solutions.body: A landing page where people can sign up and hear as soon as it opens.

solutions.title: Sign-up and login
solutions.body: Personal accounts with email and password, confirmed by email.

solutions.title: A home page for each student
solutions.body: Students land here after logging in. It's where their results by topic and practice suggestions will live.

solutions.title: Web and phone on one base
solutions.body: iOS and Android come after the web version, built on the same foundation.

mamor.name: Project Mamor
mamor.description: A Next.js website for a model agency, with statically generated model profiles. The moving backdrops are custom WebGL fragment shaders, and a keyboard-navigable search overlay filters results as you type.

solutions.title: A profile for every model
solutions.body: Height, measurements, shoe size, eye and hair colour are all in one place.

solutions.title: Full-screen search
solutions.body: Results narrow as you type, and you can step through them with the keyboard.

solutions.title: A moving backdrop on the home page
solutions.body: Surfaces that recall marble and silk take turns, which gives the page character even without photos.

solutions.title: Made for phones too
solutions.body: The pages work well on a small screen.

thrift.name: Project Thrift
thrift.description: A two-sided marketplace app for secondhand fashion. People post a style brief rather than a specific item, and others accept it as a paid quest and hunt through thrift stores for matching pieces.

solutions.title: A style, not a product
solutions.body: People describe the style they want rather than one specific item.

solutions.title: Paid quests
solutions.body: Others can accept a post as a paid quest.

solutions.title: A treasure hunt in thrift stores
solutions.body: Quest takers search thrift stores for matching pieces, which turns thrifting into a rewarded treasure hunt.

scanner.name: Project Scanner
scanner.description: A scan-to-score mobile app for food and cosmetics. It rates a product on the spot, breaks it down ingredient by ingredient and surfaces better alternatives.

solutions.title: An instant rating
solutions.body: Scan a product and see right away how healthy it is.

solutions.title: Ingredients explained
solutions.body: The app explains what each ingredient does.

solutions.title: Easy-read symbols
solutions.body: Simple symbols flag things like vegan or free-from products.

solutions.title: Better options at a glance
solutions.body: It helps people quickly find a better choice.

process.label: How we work
process.title: Clear steps, no surprises.
process.subtitle: We don't experiment with your money. We start with an assessment, begin with one small, well-defined task, and only build on what works.

assess.title: Free assessment
assess.body: We talk through your goals, look at your current tools, and map where the most time gets lost.

plan.title: Written plan, fixed price
plan.body: Exact scope, timeline, and a fixed price per phase, in writing. Bigger jobs start with a small pilot.

build.title: Built in short rounds
build.body: You see working results week by week and can steer as we go. Nothing goes live untested.

run.title: Handover and operation
run.body: We train your team, hand over full documentation, and look after the system for a monthly fee.

team.label: Team
team.title: Built by engineers. Backed by experience.
team.subtitle: We design, build and run your systems ourselves, from the first call to long after handover.

peter.name: Péter Révész
bio: His expertise covers the full product and engineering lifecycle, from customer discovery to architecting secure, scalable cloud‑native systems. He has worked at startups backed by Fusion VC and Hiventures, and on US healthcare and edtech products for enterprise clients. On a founding team, he built a platform that ran on 3,000+ enterprise sites, including Nvidia, Datadog and CrowdStrike.

kristof.name: Kristóf Rétfalvi
bio: He has several years of experience building web and mobile applications. He has worked on business web apps, US healthcare systems, real‑time video communication platforms and mobile apps. His work has included building complex features independently, technical design, and coordinating entire parts of projects. He puts a strong focus on quality execution, user experience and reliable operation.

privacy.title: Privacy Policy
privacy.intro: Your privacy matters to us. This policy explains what personal data we collect, how we use it, and how we keep it safe.

controller.title: Data controller
controller.content:
Péter Révész, as a private individual. Budapest Labs is a concept for now, not a registered business (see the Imprint).
Email: hello@budapestlabs.com

collection.title: What we collect
collection.content: When you fill out our contact form, we receive: your name, email address, phone number (if you choose to share it), business name (optional), the service you're interested in, and your message. That's it. You can also write to us directly at hello@budapestlabs.com. We don't use cookies, tracking scripts, or analytics tools of any kind.

basis.title: Why we're allowed to use it
basis.content: We handle your data because you chose to send it to us. That's your consent under EU data protection law (GDPR).

purpose.title: What we do with it
purpose.content: We use your contact details only to get back to you and talk through your idea. We will never sell, rent, or share your information with anyone for marketing or any unrelated purpose.

storage.title: How we keep it safe
storage.content: Your data is stored on encrypted servers within the European Union. Messages are kept while we're talking, plus up to 1 year afterwards, and then permanently deleted. Sooner if you ask.

thirdparty.title: Services we rely on
thirdparty.content: Our website is hosted on Vercel (vercel.com), and we use Resend (resend.com) to deliver emails from our contact form. Both providers process data on our behalf under GDPR-compliant agreements. All connections use HTTPS encryption. Vercel keeps standard server logs (IP address, timestamp, page visited), which are automatically deleted after 30 days. Your information is never shared with anyone else.

rights.title: Your rights
rights.content: Under EU law (GDPR), you can: ask to see what data we have about you; correct anything that's wrong; ask us to delete your data; limit or object to how we use it; or request a copy in a portable format. You can also withdraw your consent at any time. This won't affect anything we did before the withdrawal. Just email us at hello@budapestlabs.com and we'll get back to you within 30 days.

terms.title: Terms of Use
terms.intro: Budapest Labs is a concept for now. These terms cover the use of this website, not a service or a contract.

status.title: A concept, not a business yet
status.content: Budapest Labs is not a registered company or sole proprietorship, and has no tax number. It doesn't sell services, sign contracts, take payments, or issue invoices.

website.title: What this site is for
website.content: It shows how we'd like to work once the business is founded. The services, the way of working (free assessment, written plan, fixed price per phase) and the examples describe plans, not an offer. The chat demo answers and the AI examples are illustrations.

contact.title: If you write to us
contact.content: A message or a conversation creates no obligation for either side. We're happy to reply and talk through your idea. We'll only take on paid work once the business exists, and then only with a written contract.

future.title: Once the business is founded
future.content: We'll publish its details and full terms of service, and update the Imprint and the Privacy Policy.

brands.title: Brand names
brands.content: Products and services named on this site (for example Claude, Billingo, Shopify) are trademarks of their owners. Naming them doesn't mean a partnership or endorsement.

liability.title: Liability
liability.content: The information on this site is for general information only. We try to keep it accurate, but we're not liable for decisions based on it.

law.title: Governing law
law.content: These terms are governed by Hungarian law.

status.content: Budapest Labs is a concept for now, not a registered company or sole proprietorship. It has no registered seat, tax number or registration number. Once the business is founded, its details will be published here.
